subject: Startups
title: Robinhood's Waitlist Gambit
description: A quick, practical guide to Robinhood's Waitlist Gambit.

hook.text: Robinhood launched with a waitlist of 1 million people—before the app even existed. How?

buildup.text: The waitlist showed your position in line. Refer friends, and you'd move up. It turned waiting into a game.

discovery.text: People shared referral links obsessively. Moving from spot 500K to 10K felt like winning. Social proof was baked in.

twist.text: The product didn't exist yet. Robinhood validated demand and built a user base before writing a single trade feature.

climax.text: By launch day, Robinhood had massive demand with zero ad spend. The waitlist hack became a startup playbook staple.

punchline.text: Make people compete to wait for your product.

quiz.question: How did Robinhood incentivize referrals on its pre-launch waitlist?
options: Moving users higher in the waitlist queue
